system.name: SpikeMaskGS
system.one_liner: Dynamic-scene novel view synthesis with static and dynamic Gaussians, using a spatio-temporal fine-grained mask field and a spiking-neuron tagging field.

content.variant_note: Others and Ours drawn side by side in five of six lettered panels: two schematics of design choices, then three rendered comparisons with highlighted crops; panel (A) is the shared baseline pipeline
content.argues: Fixing two weak points of dynamic-static decomposition, inaccurate mask priors and improper tag representations, gives cleaner decomposition and better side views, fine motions and boundaries.
content.subject: The dynamic-static Gaussian pipeline, two design choices contrasted with other methods, and rendered side views, motions and boundaries.

lessons.what_to_learn: Split every panel into an Others half and an Ours half so that each design choice is contrasted on one canvas, then repeat the frame colour of each issue panel on the result panel that shows its effect. Dashed frames suit schematics and solid frames suit rendered results.
lessons.suits: Method papers that fix two or three specific weaknesses of prior work and want to show cause and effect together in one teaser.

evidence: typically assign each Gaussian primitive a dynamic–static tag and optimize them using dynamic–static mask priors (Fig. 1 A)
Current methods use an improper tag representation that optimizes continuous probabilities and uses threshold-based post-processing for discrete labels
we directly optimize a discontinuous tagging field via a Spiking Neuron, achieving cleaner decomposition and clearer boundaries

summary: The paper renders dynamic scenes with separate static and dynamic Gaussians and argues that two choices of earlier work limit this decomposition: inaccurate mask priors and improper tag representations. Figure 1 has six lettered panels. (A) draws the baseline pipeline, with mask priors supervising a tag representation that splits Gaussians into static and dynamic processing. (B) and (C), in dashed orange and teal frames, put Others beside Ours: inconsistent or temporally invariant masks against a spatio-temporal fine-grained mask field, and a sigmoid with post-processing and uncertainty against a spiking neuron with a step function. (D), (E) and (F), in solid frames of matching colours, compare rendered side views, fine motions and boundaries with red and green crops.
summary_zh: 论文用静态/动态高斯渲染动态场景，指出掩码先验不准和标签表示不当两个问题。图1含A–F六个面板：A为基线流程；B、C以橙、青虚线框并排对比Others与Ours；D–F用同色实线框展示侧视角、精细运动和边界的渲染对比与放大图。
notes: Prior order (contribution-mosaic first) changed: Others against Ours is the grammar of five of the six panels, so side-by-side-contrast leads and contribution-mosaic stays second because the panels also carry the two contributions and the results. The meaning of the circled cross in (A) and of the red and green crop boxes is read from the picture; the paper text does not explain them. The caption points from (B) to (E) and from (C) to (F), which the repeated frame colours support.
